title: A movement monitoring system for assessing restricted rodents' movements during social interaction tests
protocol: Arrange the 6 piezo-electric disks to fit into the shape of the Plexiglas plate.
Solder the outer rings of the piezo-electric disks to each other.
Cut copper foil strips and place them with the isolated part facing down to connect between the inner parts of the piezo-electric disks.
Solder all edges of the copper foil strips to the inner part of the piezo-electric disks.
Solder two more wires to one of the piezo-electric disks aimed to be closer to the 90 degrees' corner.
Position the soldered piezo-electric array in between the laminating films.
Laminate the piezo-electric array by blowing hot air (~100-150℃) using a hot air gun.
Cut the laminated film around the piezo-electric array in a triangulated shape.
Tape the edges of the assembled array to the edges of the Plexiglas plate using packaging tape.
Leave the hole in the plate uncovered.
Insert the main leading wire into the pipette tube.
Expose the leading ends of the wires using a wire striper.
Place shrink tubes on the wires.
Solder the leads on the back end of the pipette to the piezo-electric array leads.
Solder the leads on the other side to two pins of the USB female connector.
Cut a slit of about 2 mm wide and 5 mm height at the flat end of the pipette.
Insert the flat end of the pipette into the hole in the Plexiglas plate.
Tape the pipette to the Plexiglas plate to protect the wires.
Solder a two-lead wire to the corresponding pins on the USB male connector.
Connect the leads on the other side of the wire to the recording system.
Connect the movement monitoring device to one of the analog inputs of Intan RHD data acquisition board.
Start recordings with the data acquisition system.
Trigger the camera after starting the data acquisition system recordings.
Record timestamps of each frame acquired from the camera (TTL pulses).
Record piezo-electric signals during recording.
Use an Intan RHD data acquisition board for recordings at a sampling rate of 20 kHz.
Extract recorded data using codes supplied by Intan Technologies.
Analyze extracted signals using custom-made MATLAB codes written in versions 2017a-2020a.
